intro: We next tested chemical bond breaking, which forces a smooth transition from a single dominant electronic configuration around equilibrium geometry to a multiconfigurational structure at dissociation, which has been a long-standing stress test for computational methods. For simple hydrogen chains, in which two to eight hydrogen atoms are pulled apart simultaneously, our method's dissociation curves closely track near-exact reference calculations across all chain lengths tested.

Extending to real multi-bond chemistry, our method also correctly separates {molbonds} into their correct fragments [cite:kuchitsu1998-structures] [cite:huber1979-diatomic], capturing subtleties such as an avoided crossing between two dissociation pathways in acetylene that a less complete treatment could miss [cite:siegbahn1981-acetylene].

The most demanding case is the carbon dimer, C_{2}, whose quadruple bond has remained a long-standing challenge in electronic structure theory [cite:shaik2013-c2]. Our calculations reproduce near-exact benchmark energies [cite:holmes2017-shci] and match the experimentally measured bond length and binding energy [cite:martin1992-c2] [cite:huber1979-diatomic]. Across all of these cases, spanning one to four breaking bonds, the method requires no case-by-case adjustment.
chains: SSR(n,n) description of concerted dissociation of H–H bonds in hydrogen chains H_{n}. Potential energy curves (PECs) for H_{2} from SSR(2,2)/BH&HLYP/aug-cc-pVTZ (solid line), KS-DFT (dashed grey), and full configuration interaction (FCI; circles); the short dashed segment marks the energy of isolated atoms. PECs for H_{4}, H_{6} and H_{8} from SSR(n,n)/BH&HLYP compared with FCI. H_{4} uses the aug-cc-pVTZ basis set for both SSR and FCI; H_{6} and H_{8} use 6-31G*, a smaller basis set required because FCI becomes computationally intractable for larger ones. Triangles denote single-point FCI references computed with larger basis sets: aug-cc-pVDZ (H_{6}) and cc-pVDZ (H_{8}). Since FCI with a small basis set cannot fully capture the correlation energy, the FCI curves of H_{6} and H_{8} lie somewhat above the corresponding SSR curves. DFT-based methods are less sensitive to basis set size than FCI [cite:goerigk2011-benchmark] [cite:bursch2022-protocols], so the depth of the SSR minima at equilibrium geometries agrees better with the FCI single-point values obtained at the larger basis sets. Lower panels: natural occupations n_{i} of S0; dotted: R_{e} of S0.

c2h4: The ground-state PEC smoothly correlates the equilibrium geometry with the asymptotic energy of two isolated ^{3}B_{1} methylene fragments, confirming accurate ground-state double-bond dissociation; near equilibrium, SSR(4,4) matches KS DFT, but KS DFT fails qualitatively at extended bond lengths, diverging unphysically upward.

At equilibrium, SSR(4,4) predicts the vertical excitation energy to B^{1}B_{1u} at 7.85 eV, close to the TBE value of 7.93 eV [cite:veril2021-questdb]. This state dissociates into two ^{1}B_{1} methylenes; since two such states form two distinct linear combinations, a second excited state (D^{1}A_{g}) converges to the same asymptote, splitting by only 0.14 eV at 4.0 Å from in-phase/out-of-phase coupling. The A^{1}B_{2g} and C^{1}A_{g} states converge to the (^{1}A_{1})CH_{2} + (^{1}A_{1})CH_{2} limit; near equilibrium, A^{1}B_{2g} shows initial Rydberg character before an avoided crossing with a valence state of the same symmetry. All five singlet-state asymptotic energies map consistently onto the isolated-fragment energies, with minor discrepancies from differing state-averaging conditions. Overall, SSR(4,4) gives a quantitatively reliable, balanced description of multiple-bond dissociation across the full surface.
n2: Using SSR(6,6)/BH&HLYP, the N_{2} ground-state PEC evolves smoothly from equilibrium (calc.: {re} Å; exp.: {reExp} Å [cite:huber1979-diatomic]) to two isolated ground-state (^{4}S) nitrogen atoms. We did not classify excited states by symmetry or rigorously benchmark vertical excitation energies, since these depend on functional choice; nevertheless, SSR(6,6)/BH&HLYP reasonably reproduces the lowest vertical excitation and captures triple-bond dissociation with conceptual fidelity, free of unphysical artifacts or symmetry-breaking discontinuities.
c2h2: Acetylene (C_{2}H_{2}) shows analogous behavior. The pathway correlating with triple C≡C character dissociates to two CH radicals in their ^{4}Σ^{−} states [cite:siegbahn1981-acetylene]. Since isolated CH's ground state is ^{2}Π, an avoided crossing occurs between pathways converging to the (^{4}Σ^{−})CH + (^{4}Σ^{−})CH and (^{2}Π)CH + (^{2}Π)CH asymptotes [cite:siegbahn1981-acetylene]. SSR(6,6) captures this crossing accurately, with the ^{1}Σ_{g}^{+} PECs converging smoothly to their limits after traversing the crossing region. Together, these results show REKS/SSR delivers a chemically sound description of multiple-bond cleavage while resolving fine topological features of complex dissociation pathways.
c2: SSR(6,6) accurately maps the two lowest states (X^{1}Σ_{g}^{+} and a^{3}Π_{u}), aligning closely with the reference points. The calculated singlet-triplet splitting (T_{e}) is exceptionally narrow at 0.03 eV, close to the experimental 0.09 eV [cite:martin1992-c2]. The A^{1}Π_{u} excited state's structure and energetics also agree reasonably with experiment. SSR underestimates the B^{1}Δ_{g} T_{e} by ∼{dTeB} eV, though its PEC minimum matches the experimental R_{e} well.

This ability to capture quadruple-bond dissociation reflects the localized nature of SSR's correlation treatment: non-dynamic correlation within only three – not four – electron pairs suffices to describe C_{2} bond cleavage. Near equilibrium, C–C stabilization arises mainly from configuration mixing via 2σ_{u} → 3σ_{g} promotion, seen as fractional occupations in the two σ orbitals, while the π orbitals remain largely doubly occupied (1π_{u}) or empty (1π_{g}).

As the bond elongates, the σ occupations converge to integer values of two (2σ_{u}) and zero (3σ_{g}), neutralizing σ-bonding, while the π manifold redistributes to single occupancy of bonding and anti-bonding orbitals – homolytic cleavage of the two π bonds. Thus, non-dynamic correlation within three electron pairs (one σ, two π) suffices to model the quadruple-bond dissociation, consistent with chemical intuition.

SSR(6,6) accurately reproduces the ground- and excited-state character of this notoriously difficult molecule, yielding a dissociation energy (D_{e}) of {de} eV, in excellent agreement with the experimental 6.32±0.2 eV [cite:huber1979-diatomic].

methods.chain: The REKS/SSR calculations for the hydrogen chains were executed using a state-averaged ensemble that included the PPS1 configuration and all OSSx configurations generated within the same GVB orbital pairing scheme. To ensure stable SCF convergence, a high-spin determinant was incorporated into the ensembles. All density functional calculations utilized the BH&HLYP functional. For the REKS/SSR calculations, initial guess orbitals were generated via standard KS-DFT calculations using the identical density functional and basis set. Potential energy curves were scanned {scan}. Additionally, reference full configuration interaction calculations were carried out using the Psi4 package.
methods.chainNoFci: The REKS/SSR calculations for the hydrogen chains were executed using a state-averaged ensemble that included the PPS1 configuration and all OSSx configurations generated within the same GVB orbital pairing scheme. To ensure stable SCF convergence, a high-spin determinant was incorporated into the ensembles. All density functional calculations utilized the BH&HLYP functional. For the REKS/SSR calculations, initial guess orbitals were generated via standard KS-DFT calculations using the identical density functional and basis set. Potential energy curves were scanned {scan}.
methods.c2h4: For ethylene, SA-REKS(4,4) orbital optimization utilized a four-state ensemble comprising the PPS1, OSS1, and OSS2 singlet configurations alongside a high-spin (HS) quintet electronic configuration. Incorporating the high-spin quintet state accelerates SCF convergence and minimizes the total iteration count. The subsequent SI step included 18 configurations to comprehensively span all physical configurations arising from the two coupling schemes within the (4,4) active space. For the dissociation fragments, singlet state energies of CH_{2} were computed using SSR(2,2) calculations restricted to the PPS1 and OSS1 configurations, whereas the ground triplet state was modelled via the spin-restricted open-shell Kohn-Sham (ROKS) method. All electronic structure calculations were performed using the BH&HLYP density functional paired with the aug-cc-pVTZ basis set. The initial guess orbitals were obtained in a standard KS DFT calculation with the same density functional and basis set. The potential energy curves were scanned {scan}.
methods.c2h2: The SSR(6,6) calculations for N_{2} and C_{2}H_{2} were performed using a five-state ensemble – comprising PPS1, OSS1, OSS2, OSS3, and HS – for orbital optimization, combined with a complete set of configurations for the state-interaction stage. Dissociation fragments were computed via the ROKS high-spin method. All simulations utilized the BH&HLYP density functional alongside the aug-cc-pVTZ basis set.
methods.n2: The SSR(6,6) calculations for N_{2} and C_{2}H_{2} were performed using a five-state ensemble – comprising PPS1, OSS1, OSS2, OSS3, and HS – for orbital optimization, combined with a complete set of configurations for the state-interaction stage. Dissociation fragments were computed via the ROKS high-spin method. All simulations utilized the BH&HLYP density functional alongside the aug-cc-pVTZ basis set.
methods.c2: The SA-REKS(6,6) orbital optimizations for C_{2} were performed using a nine-state ensemble. In addition to the five configurations shared with N_{2} and C_{2}H_{2}, this ensemble included four triplet configurations generated by one-electron spin-flip transitions from the 1π_{u} to 3σ_{g} orbitals. These transitions arise across all orbital coupling schemes compatible with ^{3}Π_{u} total symmetry. At the subsequent state-interaction stage, complete sets of singlet and triplet configurations were utilized. To determine the dissociation energy, the energies of isolated carbon atoms were calculated via the SSR(4,4) method. This was achieved by assigning one 2s and two 2p orbitals to the active space, followed by an orbital optimization over an ensemble of PPS1, OSS1, OSS2, and HS states. The resulting energies for the ^{3}P triplet state of carbon – comprising two degenerate components with m_{S} = 0 and m_{L} = ±1 at −37.8330687 Hartree – differ from the ROKS triplet state energy (−37.8300017 Hartree) by roughly 0.08 eV. All calculations were carried out using the M08-SO density functional paired with the cc-pV5Z basis set.
